questions.q: Which of the following is a bound morpheme?
questions.explanation: '-ness' cannot stand alone and must be attached to a root.

questions.q: The word 'brunch' is an example of:
questions.explanation: Blending combines parts of two words (breakfast + lunch).

questions.q: What type of morpheme changes the grammatical category of a word?
questions.explanation: Derivational morphemes change the word class (e.g., happy -> happiness).
Clipping is shortening a longer word without changing its meaning.

questions.q: The '-ed' in 'walked' is an example of what kind of morpheme?
questions.explanation: '-ed' shows tense and is therefore an inflectional morpheme.
Acronyms are formed from initial letters and pronounced as a single word.
Compounding joins two free morphemes together.

questions.q: How many morphemes are in the word 'unbelievable'?
Creating the verb 'edit' from the noun 'editor' is an example of:
questions.explanation: Backformation removes an apparent affix to create a new word.

questions.q: Using 'google' as a verb ('I will google it') is an example of:
questions.explanation: Conversion changes a word's class without adding any affixes.
